basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 14.' and it opens '(Vers. 14.) Et vocavit Abraham nomen loci illius, Dominus videt: ut dicant hodie, in'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 14.) Et vocavit Abraham nomen loci illius, Dominus videt: ut dicant hodie, in monte Dominus videt. Pro eo quod hic habet videt, in Hebraeo scriptum est, videbitur. Hoc autem apud Hebraeos exivit in proverbium, ut si quando in angustia constituti sunt, et Domini optant auxilio sublevari, dicant, In monte Dominus videbitur: hoc est, sicut Abrahae misertus est, miserebitur et nostri. Unde et in signum dati arietis solent etiam nunc cornu clangere.
